title: Logs that know their trace
summary: ILogger message templates, scopes, the OpenTelemetry logging provider, and the trace id that ties a log line to its request.

steps.title: Structured logs through OpenTelemetry
body: Keep using `ILogger`; add the OpenTelemetry provider with `.WithLogging()` on the same builder. Each log record then carries:
- the **trace id and span id** of `Activity.Current` when it was written (the link to the trace, for free);
- the resource (`service.name`...), the category, the severity;
- the **message template** as the body and each placeholder as a typed **attribute**.
```csharp
log.LogInformation("Order {OrderId} placed for {Amount}", order.Id, order.Total);   // good: template + attributes
log.LogInformation($"Order {order.Id} placed for {order.Total}");                     // bad: a new message per order
With the template, the backend can group all "Order {OrderId} placed" lines, filter `OrderId = 8812`, and the text is never parsed.
With interpolation every line is a different string, the values are lost as fields, and the string is built even when the level is
off. (The `CA2254` analyzer warns about it. For hot paths, `[LoggerMessage]` source-generated methods avoid boxing as well.)
**Scopes** add context to every line inside them: `using (log.BeginScope(new Dictionary<string, object> { ["app.tenant"] = tenant }))`.
The OpenTelemetry provider exports them only with `IncludeScopes = true`:
```csharp
.WithLogging(logging => { }, options => options.IncludeScopes = true)

steps.explain: Only the template keeps `OrderId` and `Amount` as separate, typed fields and one stable message shape. `Console.WriteLine` bypasses logging entirely: no level, no trace id, no export.

steps.prompt: What does this print? (The formatter fills placeholders by position, not by name.)
steps.explain: That is how `ILogger` renders the message for humans; the exporter sends the template (`{OriginalFormat}`) and `OrderId = 8812`, `Amount = 37.5` as attributes. Placeholders are positional: naming them `{Amount} {OrderId}` with the arguments in the old order silently swaps the fields.

steps.title: Log inside the request, with a template and a scope
prompt: - the OpenTelemetry logging provider (`.WithLogging(...)`) with **scopes included**;
- in `POST /orders/{id:int}?tenant=...&amount=...`, open a **scope** with `app.tenant` = the tenant, and inside it log at
**Information** with exactly this template: **`Order {OrderId} placed for {Amount}`**, passing `id` (an int) and `amount` (a double);
Inject `ILogger<Program>` into the handler. Tracing is already on, so the request has a server span: your log record must carry its
starter: app.MapPost("/orders/{id:int}", (int id, string tenant, double amount) => Results.Ok());
solution: app.MapPost("/orders/{id:int}", (int id, string tenant, double amount, ILogger<Program> log) =>
hints: `.WithLogging(logging => { }, options => options.IncludeScopes = true)` on the OpenTelemetry builder.
`using (log.BeginScope(new Dictionary<string, object> { ["app.tenant"] = tenant })) log.LogInformation("Order {OrderId} placed for {Amount}", id, amount);`
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
var r = await http.PostAsync("/orders/8812?tenant=acme&amount=37.5", null);
DojoWeb.Status("POST answers 200", 200, r);
var server = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.Kind == ActivityKind.Server);
DojoOtel.Flush();
var log = DojoOtel.Logs.FirstOrDefault(l => l.Template?.Contains("placed") == true);
Dojo.Check("a log record was exported", log is not null, "Records: " + string.Join(" | ", DojoOtel.Logs.Select(l => l.Template)) + ". Is WithLogging() on the builder?");
if (log is null) return;
Dojo.Eq("the body is the template, not the rendered text", "Order {OrderId} placed for {Amount}", log.Template);
Dojo.Eq("level Information", "Information", log.Level.ToString());
Dojo.Check("OrderId is the int 8812", log.Attributes.GetValueOrDefault("OrderId") is int dojoId && dojoId == 8812, "got " + log.Attributes.GetValueOrDefault("OrderId"));
Dojo.Check("Amount is the double 37.5", log.Attributes.GetValueOrDefault("Amount") is double dojoAmt && dojoAmt == 37.5, "got " + log.Attributes.GetValueOrDefault("Amount")?.GetType().Name);
Dojo.Eq("the scope's app.tenant is exported", "acme", log.Attributes.GetValueOrDefault("app.tenant") as string);
Dojo.Eq("the record carries the request's trace id", server?.TraceId.ToHexString(), log.TraceId);
Dojo.Eq("and the server span's span id", server?.SpanId.ToHexString(), log.SpanId);

steps.title: Give users the trace id
body: When a request fails, put the trace id in the error response. Support gets "trace 46ae7e54..." instead of "it broke around three",
and on-call opens exactly that trace and its logs. ASP.NET Core's problem details already add a `traceId` when you use
`AddProblemDetails()`; by hand:
```csharp
catch (PaymentException ex)
log.LogError(ex, "Payment failed for order {OrderId}", id);     // the exception travels with the record
Activity.Current?.AddException(ex);                               // and as an event on the span
return Results.Problem("Payment failed", statusCode: 502,
extensions: new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["traceId"] = Activity.Current?.TraceId.ToString() });
Pass the exception as the **first argument** of `LogError`, never inside the template: then the exporter sends `exception.type`,
`exception.message` and `exception.stacktrace` as fields.

steps.prompt: Order the catch block so the failure is logged and traced before the response is returned.

steps.title: A failure the support desk can quote
prompt: `POST /pay/{id:int}` calls `Payments.Charge(id)`, which throws `InvalidOperationException("card declined")` for odd ids (both are
in the starter). Catch it and:
- log at **Error** with the exception as the first argument and the template **`Payment failed for order {OrderId}`**;
- record the exception on the current span (`AddException`) and set the span status to **Error**;
- answer **502** with a problem-details body whose extension **`traceId`** is the current trace id.
Even ids succeed with `200`. Keep tracing and logging on (the starter has both).
starter: public static void Charge(int id) { if (id % 2 == 1) throw new InvalidOperationException("card declined"); }
solution: public static void Charge(int id) { if (id % 2 == 1) throw new InvalidOperationException("card declined"); }
hints: Wrap the call in `try`/`catch (InvalidOperationException ex)`; `Activity.Current` is the server span of this request.
`Results.Problem("Payment failed", statusCode: 502, extensions: new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["traceId"] = Activity.Current?.TraceId.ToString() })`
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
DojoWeb.Status("an even id is paid", 200, await http.PostAsync("/pay/2", null));
var r = await http.PostAsync("/pay/7", null);
DojoWeb.Status("an odd id answers 502", 502, r);
var traceId = DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(r), "traceId");
Dojo.Check("the body carries a traceId", traceId is { Length: 32 }, "got " + (traceId ?? "nothing"));
var server = await DojoOtel.Span(a => a.Kind == ActivityKind.Server && a.TraceId.ToHexString() == traceId);
Dojo.Check("it is the trace of this request", server is not null, "");
Dojo.Eq("the span status is Error", "Error", server?.Status.ToString());
Dojo.Check("the exception is an event on the span", server?.Events.Any(e => e.Name == "exception") == true, "events: " + string.Join(",", server?.Events.Select(e => e.Name) ?? []));
DojoOtel.Flush();
var log = DojoOtel.Logs.FirstOrDefault(l => l.Level == Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LogLevel.Error);
Dojo.Eq("an Error record with the template", "Payment failed for order {OrderId}", log?.Template);
Dojo.Eq("the exception travels with the record", "InvalidOperationException", log?.Exception);
Dojo.Eq("the record has the same trace id", traceId, log?.TraceId);
